subject: english-literature
title: Genette's Toolkit
welcome_lead: Gérard Genette's terminology gave narratology its sharpest tools. Stock the workbench.
meta_desc: Gérard Genette's narratology — focalisation, order, duration — at A-Level English Literature.
final_note: You have stocked the narratological toolkit — focalisation, order and voice ready to deploy.

concepts.def: Foundational narratological study analysing Proust through systematic categories.
Whose perspective filters narrative information — zero, internal or external.
Who speaks — heterodiegetic (outside) or homodiegetic (inside) the story.
The relation between story-time and discourse-time — analepsis (flashback), prolepsis (flash-forward).
How story-time maps to discourse-time — scene, summary, ellipsis, pause.
How often events are told relative to occurrence — singulative, repetitive, iterative.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Genette's heterodiegetic narrator stands outside the story (omniscient third); the homodiegetic narrator is inside (first person).

The autodiegetic narrator is a homodiegetic narrator who is the protagonist (David Copperfield).
Genette separates voice from focalisation. Even a heterodiegetic narrator can use internal focalisation — filtering the scene through one character's senses.
Order: events may be told out of sequence (analepsis, prolepsis). Duration: a single morning may take 100 pages (Mrs Dalloway) or be summarised in a sentence.

numericals.q: Genette identified how many types of focalisation?

free_texts.q: A first-person narrator who is also the protagonist is termed ____.
